A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PointCNN++ work, with matching core methods and experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison. v1 includes supplementary Sections F–H; the supplied v3 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational benchmarks, KITTI and 3DMatch registration results, and supplementary hardware, scalability and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original computational and registration results and adds a nuScenes semantic-segmentation experiment.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 4.1 retain the point-centric convolution, neighborhood construction, sampling procedures and MVMR/VVOR kernels. The segmentation experiment applies the existing operator. Omission of supplementary pseudocode and implementation listings does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Section 4.4 adds nuScenes semantic segmentation, extending evaluation to scene understanding beyond registration and computational benchmarking. S3DIS performance benchmarks and KITTI/3DMatch registration remain.

E2.justification: fVDB is removed from the main efficiency comparisons in Figures 3–5. PointCNN gains actual latency results in Figures 4–5, whereas v1 merely lists its implementation in Table C. These changes materially alter the efficiency comparator set; registration comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new segmentation evaluation uses a ResUNet2 backbone, MSC pre-training, batch size 3, controlled operator replacement, and mIoU, mAcc, memory and iteration-time measurements. The retained RTX 4090 performance benchmark specifies the same settings. Missing supplementary registration settings represent lost documentation, not demonstrated changes to those experiments.

E4.justification: v3 omits the A800/L20/V100 validation, memory-scaling stress test and 3DMatch qualitative cases from v1 Sections F–G and Figures G–K. These tested hardware generality, scalability limits and alignment behavior. The degraded-operator comparison and Table 2 sample-count sweep remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 independent timing runs per scene and retain the KITTI mean/standard-deviation reporting. No new seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises PointCNN++ FMR/IR values: the 250-sample column changes from 99.2/53.4 to 99.1/64.1, while registration recalls and Table 1 remain unchanged. Figure 5 changes its forward/backward timings from 60.4/75.5 to 61.9/77.8 ms. Table 3 adds nuScenes results, including 78.2% versus MinkowskiEngine's 74.4% mIoU. The backbone-memory and supplementary results are omitted.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the expected unique-index calculation and the memory-access analysis are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the accuracy claim to semantic segmentation, and the introduction newly claims state-of-the-art segmentation results. The central point-native convolution and precision–efficiency contributions, including the conclusion, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 removes the discussion of fVDB's inference/training tradeoff and the supplement's explanations of hardware independence and extreme-scale feasibility. It adds segmentation-based applicability arguments and a qualification explaining why TensorFlow PointCNN memory measurements are excluded from PyTorch comparisons. These substantially revise the interpretation accompanying the efficiency evidence.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the open-source promise with a public-repository statement and link. However, it omits Table C's implementation versions, detailed registration splits/preprocessing/thresholds, the 50,000-iteration RANSAC configuration, Algorithm B and Triton/PyTorch Listings 1–3. References to supplementary implementation material remain despite its absence from this PDF.

R1.justification: The nuScenes dataset paper is added to support the new experiment. The existing related-work discussion and other cited works are retained, including fVDB; reference renumbering and bibliographic formatting do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain unchanged. Editing is concentrated in the abstract/introduction and Section 4.2, with a new Section 4.4, acknowledgments and updated author/contact information. Supplementary Sections F–H are omitted.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 shrink from full-width displays to small single-column plots with revised legends and axes. Figure 5 loses its memory panel, Table 3 is added, and supplementary tables, figures and listings disappear. Figure 6 retains the same images but gains an explanation of error coloring and the 0.1 m display threshold.

improvement.justification: The controlled nuScenes experiment provides useful evidence of broader applicability, and the repository link improves access information. However, v3 removes fVDB, which had faster inference than PointCNN++ in v1, together with hardware/scalability validation and substantial reproducibility documentation. These gains and losses affect central aspects of the paper, and the supplied PDFs do not support a reliable net judgment of improvement.
